description: Server-side request forgery: the caller choosing which machine the application talks to from inside the network. The second route passes untrusted data into a URL whose host is already fixed by a literal, leaving only a path segment, and is not a finding. The third sends caller data to a fixed destination, which is a different judgement about a different argument of the same call. The stated cost of that discriminator is a false negative on `"https://" + host`, which is composed and genuinely caller-chosen; that shape is rarer than a fixed base with a variable path, and a miss is the cheaper error than flooding every service that builds a URL from an id.

expected.note: the whole destination comes from the caller
